title: Lan Na Kingdom
capsule: The Lan Na Kingdom was founded by King Mangrai, who established Chiang Mai as its capital in 1296 and consolidated control over the highland valleys of what is now northern Thailand. At its peak in the fifteenth century under King Tilokaraj (r. 1441–1487), Lan Na hosted the Eighth Buddhist Council (1477), produced a flourishing of Theravada scholarship and temple architecture, and repulsed repeated Ayutthayan invasions. Burmese Taungoo forces under Bayinnaung conquered Chiang Mai in 1558, ending independent Lan Na rule; the kingdom thereafter functioned as a Burmese vassal state until Siamese-assisted restoration in 1775.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territorial boundaries around the northern Thai highlands are reasonably well attested via Mangrai chronicles and Burmese annals; peripheral frontier zones with Ayutthaya and Shan states are more ambiguous.
